subject: Invoice overdue
top_finding: Attachment is a program disguised as something else

message.subject: Invoice overdue
message.excerpt: Please see the attached invoice and pay before your account is suspended.

findings.title: Attachment is a program disguised as something else
evidence: Invoice_7487.doc.js is named like a .js file but its contents are a PE executable
findings.lesson: The file's contents didn't match its name. That mismatch is deliberate.

findings.title: Attachment hides its real extension
evidence: Invoice_7487.doc.js has a document-style name over a .js file
findings.lesson: 'invoice.pdf.exe' is a program wearing a PDF's name. Turn on file extensions and read to the end.

findings.title: Sender domain imitates a known domain
evidence: Sender domain dhl-billing[.]example wraps the name from dhl[.]com in extra words (imitating DHL)
findings.lesson: Read the domain letter by letter. Attackers register names that look right at a glance.

findings.title: Attachment can run code
evidence: Invoice_7487.doc.js (66 bytes) has an executable extension (.js)
findings.lesson: Files like .exe, .js, .iso or .lnk run programs. Real colleagues don't send those.

findings.title: Sender failed DMARC
evidence: DMARC failed for dhl-billing[.]example (domain policy: reject)
findings.lesson: A failed sender check means the message may be forged. If it claims to be from someone you know, confirm with them another way.

findings.title: Money request with warning signs
evidence: Money-related wording ("invoice") combined with urgent wording
findings.lesson: Requests to move money or change bank details need a second channel. Call the person on a number you already have.

findings.title: SPF or DKIM check failed
evidence: SPF did not pass for dhl-billing[.]example
findings.lesson: Real mail from a company is signed. Failed signatures are one more reason to slow down.
